name: spine-backfill-reconcile
body:
SPINE BACKFILL — implemented-by ownership of the CLI and cmd code [autonomous].

SOURCE / FINDING: `implemented-by` had been used as a sparse sample of representative functions (only ~38 source functions were claimed by any solution component), while the verify gate reads the edges as complete ownership. Core CLI entry points had no owner at all (`internal/cli.runStart`, `runTemplates`, `runUpgrade`), no component owned `cmd/kalide/main.go`, and `cli-templates` / `deck-renderer` were anchored around a single function each (see solution.note.nested-sections-coverage-reconcile).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (deterministic): every non-test Go source file under `internal/` and `cmd/` is owned by at least one `solution.component`, directly (`implemented-by → File`) or through at least one of its functions.

EDITS:
- CLI: added File-level implemented-by so the command surface is owned end to end — cmd/kalide/main.go, internal/cli/cli.go (Run), init.go (runInit), initlibrary.go (runInitLibrary), start.go (runStart) → solution.component.cli-commands; internal/cli/templates.go (runTemplates and the printers) → solution.component.cli-templates; internal/cli/upgrade.go (runUpgrade) → solution.component.upgrade. Added the named entry-point function anchors runStart, runTemplates and runUpgrade alongside the files.
- REMOVED the stale placeholder implemented-by solution.component.upgrade → internal/cli.Run. Run is the shared dispatcher owned by cli-commands (it dispatches to every command), not upgrade's entry point; upgrade now anchors on its real code (runUpgrade, internal/scaffold/Upgrade and the migration/refresh halves).
- Upgrade: added File-level implemented-by internal/scaffold/{catalog,migrate,refresh,upgrade}.go (all part of the `kalide upgrade` in-place migration), alongside the existing function anchors.
- Render tier: added File-level implemented-by internal/render/deck.go → solution.component.deck-renderer (whole-deck assembly: RenderDeck, renderDeckSlide, themeStylesheet, insertBeforeSectionClose) and internal/render/render.go → solution.component.renderer (per-slide/section execution). This confirms deck-renderer honestly owns deck.go.
- Packages mapped by File-level implemented-by to their existing components: internal/deck/{config,slides}.go → deck-loader; internal/mdcheck/{check,issue,link,walk}.go → markdown-validator; internal/server/{assets,media,reload,server,themecss}.go → http-server; internal/server/gallery.go → templates-gallery; internal/slide/{parse,catalogue}.go → slide-parser; internal/suggest/suggest.go and internal/validate/{examples,links,validate,validator}.go → deck-validator; internal/template/{checkbody,checkvalues,format,manifest,registry,section,template}.go → template-registry; internal/template/{examplecheck,library,libraryerror,loadlibrary,registrylibrary,resolve}.go → template-library-loader; internal/theme/{load,theme}.go → theme-registry; internal/watch/watch.go → file-watcher; internal/scaffold/libraryguide.go → agent-guide.
- Genuinely shared files keep function-level ownership (no whole-file claim): internal/scaffold/{scaffold,external,library,helloseed}.go are written by both the seed scaffolder (init-seed) and the embedded author-guide writers (agent-guide) — added init-seed → scaffold.InitExternal and scaffold.InitLibrary so both owners are represented; internal/template/media.go is both the reserved-prefix source of truth (template-library-loader: MediaURLPrefix / ThemeURLPrefix / cleanMediaPath) and the documented layout func map (added template-registry → template.LayoutFuncMap).

RESULT (queried on this branch): 0 unowned non-test Go files under internal/ and cmd/; 55 files each owned by ≥1 component. Multiply-owned files (all genuinely shared): internal/scaffold/scaffold.go, internal/scaffold/external.go, internal/scaffold/library.go, internal/scaffold/helloseed.go (init-seed + agent-guide); internal/template/media.go (template-library-loader + template-registry).

NOT MAPPABLE: the change-set brief named `runCLI`, `runUpgradeCLI`, `runUpgradeInDir` and `runUpgradeExpect`; none exists in the scanned graph. The single upgrade CLI handler is internal/cli.runUpgrade, which now carries the edge.
